question: If \(a\) and \(b\) are digits for which \[ \begin{array}{r} 2a\\[-2pt] {}\times b3\\ \hline 69\\ 92\phantom0\\ \hline 989 \end{array} \] then \(a+b=\)
solution:
The first partial product comes from multiplying the top two-digit number by the units digit \(3\). Thus the top number is
\[
69\div3=23,
\]
which gives \(a=3\).

The second partial product is shifted one place to the left because \(b\) is the tens digit. Its unshifted value is \(92\), so
\[
b=92\div23=4.
\]
These digits agree with the final product, since \(23\times43=69+920=989\). Therefore \(a+b=3+4=7\), choice C.

edges.reason: Tens-and-ones composition includes the meaning of a teen number as one ten and units. This overlapping place-value content is necessary without prescribing the historical order of lessons.

Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.
The explicitly written two-digit-by-two-digit algorithm computes one partial product for each single-digit multiplier; the multi-digit by one-digit procedure supplies those parts.
